title: A Statistical Framework for Learning Preferences from the Past
summary: In many real-world settings such as online recommendation or consumer choice modeling, individuals make repeated choices from a fixed set of options. Accurately estimating their underlying preferences is essential for generating personalized future recommendations. Probabilistic models for understanding user choice behavior from past decisions can serve as a valuable addition to existing recommender systems and choice prediction methods.
